# Consumer app: project rules

Status: project rules. The app has not been built yet, so technical steps are `unverified` unless marked.

For how to build Databricks Apps, use the official skills (`databricks-apps`, `databricks-apps-python`, `databricks-app-design`). List them with `databricks aitools list`; installing them follows skill `write-contract`. These project rules win over general examples.

## Audience

People who consume the data. Operational monitoring belongs to the dashboard (skill `project-dashboard`).

## Rules

- Read gold tables only, through the SQL warehouse.
- Use parameterized queries. Never build SQL by joining user input into text.
- Every KPI shows its definition, period, source date and how many records were left out for missing data.
- Never count a value twice when a contract has several entities, suppliers, categories or places.
- No personal data about individuals.
- Neutral language: an unusual value is something to investigate, not proof of wrongdoing.
- No secrets in code or configuration. The app uses its own identity; grant it only what it needs.
- KPI calculations and query builders are plain functions with tests.

## Deployment (`from-docs`)

- Declare the app as a bundle resource.
- `databricks bundle deploy -t dev` uploads the code but does not restart the app. Then run `databricks bundle run <app-resource> -t dev`.
- App names are unique in a workspace.
- Free Edition: up to 3 apps, and an app stops 24 hours after it is started, updated or redeployed.
